headline_marked: [[Yami Gautam wins Best Actress]] at 72nd National Film Awards for 'Article 370'
headline: Yami Gautam wins Best Actress at 72nd National Film Awards for 'Article 370'
summary: Bollywood actress Yami Gautam has been honored with the Best Actress award at the 72nd National Film Awards for her role in 'Article 370'. The film also secured the Best Feature Film award, marking a double triumph.
details: "Every journey has a moment that reminds you why you never gave up. Today, that moment has arrived in my life. Receiving a National Film Award is an honor I will cherish forever," an emotional Yami Gautam shared after winning Best Actress at India's 72nd National Film Awards. The Bollywood actress earned this recognition for her performance in the 2024 film 'Article 370', which also secured the Best Feature Film award, marking a double triumph for the team.

Yami attributed the national award to her perseverance, determination, and unwavering faith in acting. Daughter of popular Punjabi filmmaker Mukesh Gautam, Yami grew up with a disciplined and grounded upbringing, away from the typical glamour of the film industry, a lifestyle she maintains even today.

Her journey began on the small screen, debuting in the 2008 series 'Chand Ke Paar Chalo'. Despite her father's background, she made her big-screen debut with a Kannada film before gaining widespread attention in her debut Hindi film, 'Vicky Donor'. She has since worked in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, and Malayalam cinema, notably earning acclaim for her role opposite Hrithik Roshan in 'Kaabil'.

Yami's career has steadily progressed, with her talent shining across various platforms, including successful OTT projects like 'Uri: The Surgical Strike', 'Bala', and 'A Thursday'. She constantly strives to explore herself as an actress, believing that work is her religion and honesty is paramount in her craft.

When choosing a project, Yami prioritizes the script, stating that the "sincere feeling" from the first read guides her decision, favoring realistic stories, compelling characters, and strong directors. She described the Best Actress recognition as the result of 14 years of dedicated work, where she let her performance speak for itself.

She emphasized that 'Article 370' was a story she deeply believed in, and the award is not an end but "the beginning of an even greater responsibility." Her goal now is to enrich herself, take risks, and tell stories that truly matter, encouraging others never to lose faith in their own journeys.

In her personal life, Yami married filmmaker Aditya Dhar in 2021 and welcomed their son, Vedavid, in 2024. Alongside her successful acting career, she leads a happy and balanced family life, maintaining a simple existence away from Bollywood's glitz, considering her family her greatest strength.

headline_marked: Cumilla court [[orders DNA tests for two more]] in Tonu murder probe
headline: Cumilla court orders DNA tests for two more in Tonu murder probe
summary: A Cumilla court has ordered DNA tests for two former army personnel in connection with the long-running investigation into the murder of Sohagi Jahan Tonu. The order, issued on July 16, was confirmed yesterday.
details: A Cumilla court has ordered DNA tests for two more individuals in connection with the highly publicized murder investigation of Sohagi Jahan Tonu. This development marks a significant step in the ongoing probe into the student's death.

The order was issued on July 16 by Senior Assistant Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque of the Cumilla Sadar Court. The matter was confirmed yesterday by Sadequr Rahman, an inspector at the Chief Judicial Magistrate’s Court in Cumilla.

The two individuals named in the order are former army personnel Zahidul Islam, 41, from Meghai village in Sirajganj, and Faisal Ahmed Rabbi, 32, from Lakkhinagar-Rajapur area in Cumilla Sadar South upazila. Their involvement in the case is now under further scrutiny.

According to court documents, the order was issued following a petition by Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) Inspector Tarikul Islam, who is the investigating officer in the Tonu murder case. Inspector Islam confirmed he sought court approval for the DNA samples.

Court sources have indicated that the two individuals, Zahidul Islam and Faisal Ahmed Rabbi, are not currently in police custody. The investigation continues as authorities seek to gather crucial evidence.
